# QB2 Guide

> Interactive guide to the Tenstorrent Quietbox 2 — from first boot to first model and beyond. Four choose-your-own-adventure paths, organized around what you want to do.

## Site

- [Home](https://docs.tenstorrent.com/tt-quietbox2-guide/): Landing page with SVG Venn diagram path chooser

## Paths

- [Explore](/first-timer/): Explore Tenstorrent hardware & software for the first time. Covers unboxing, first boot, hardware verification, stack installation, first model run, and the unified `tt-cli` (`tt`) tool for install/update/serve. Fully written.
- [Run & build](/ml-practitioner/): Run and build on top of models. Covers the model zoo, vLLM deployment, and performance tuning. Fully written.
- [Tinker](/builder-hacker/): Tinker with models and the software & hardware stack — write kernels and go deep. Covers TT-Metal architecture, kernel writing, TT-Lang, and profiling. Fully written.
- [Customize](/tinkerer/): Customize your workstation and make it truly your own. Covers LEDs, demos, Ubuntu customization, break-and-fix recovery, and community. Fully written.

## Hardware

The Tenstorrent Quietbox 2 (QB2) contains:
- 2× Blackhole p300c cards (4 Blackhole chips total)
- Connected via PCIe as 4 independent devices
- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS pre-installed
- Tenstorrent software stack pre-installed (drivers, tt-smi/tt-flash, TT-Metalium and
  tt-inference-server containers, tt-studio)
- No tt-metal source tree and no `~/tt-metal` at all — TT-Metalium ships as a container

## Key Facts

- The `tt` CLI is the front door: `tt device status` (hardware), `tt update` (install/upgrade to
  the tested golden set; `tt self update` upgrades `tt`), `tt model list|info|pull|ps|curl|stop`,
  `tt serve <model>`, `tt launch <client>`. PyPI package is `tenstorrent`. Preview with `--dry-run`
- Check hardware: `tt device status` — 4 rows (`p300c`, `DRAM True`) on a healthy QB2; `tt-smi -s`
  is the lower-level JSON
- Happy path: `tt update`, `tt model login`, `tt serve Qwen3-32B` (default port 20000, served id
  `Qwen/Qwen3-32B`), `tt model curl "..."`, `tt launch openwebui`
- TTNN environment: run `tt-metalium` (container wrapper in `~/.local/bin`). TTNN is on the
  container's default `python3` (`/opt/venv/bin/python3`) — there is no venv to activate
- `~/.tenstorrent-venv` holds only the hardware tooling (tt-smi, tt-flash) — not vLLM, not `hf`
- `tt serve` runs tt-inference-server from `tt`'s own pinned copy under
  `~/.local/share/tenstorrent/tools/`, not the older `~/.local/lib/tt-inference-server` checkout
- Starter model for the direct TTNN path: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (no license gate, 1.5 GB). It is
  **not** in tt-inference-server's model list, so it cannot be served via `run.py`; for serving,
  start with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct or the pre-cached Qwen3-32B
- Pre-cached Qwen3-32B is at `~/data/tt-cache/volume_id_tt_transformers-Qwen3-32B-vqb2_launch/`
  (tt-inference-server persistent volume, not an HF cache). `tt serve` reuses it only if a
  directory named `volume_id_tt_transformers-Qwen3-32B-v<spec version>` exists (`v0.17.0` at golden
  v3.0.0): check `tt serve Qwen3-32B --dry-run` for `pre-seeded volume`, else symlink the name
- Symlinks: in the `tt-metalium` container `$HOME` is mounted at `/home/user`; relative links inside
  home resolve, absolute links and links out of home dangle
- Multi-device API: use `ttnn.CreateDevices` / `ttnn.CloseDevices` (not individual open/close)
- `TT_METAL_ARCH_NAME` must be `blackhole` for QB2
